issue_context.title: System.Text.Json: Make the Utf8JsonWriter always insert newlines between the end of comments and the start of arrays or objects
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

Hi @Fydar, and thanks for writing such a detailed proposal. Superficially this seems like a reasonable change to me, although I defer to @GrabYourPitchforks, @layomia and @ahsonkhan who might be more aware of potential pitfalls.

Changing the output JSON format is typically a breaking change and this request is somewhat an edge case (using comments which isn't valid JSON per RFC, with indented). There isn't a clear set of rules for the output here, and as stated in the issue, could be a bit controversial, so such a change should require substantive rationale/benefit and some more customer requests, before prioritizing it, imo.

Does the `// comment` style of comment have this concern as well?

> Does the `// comment` style of comment have this concern as well?

I believe there currently is no way to create single-line (or `// comment`) comments using the `Utf8JsonWriter`.

I would like to see a WriteNewLine() method added to the Utf8JsonWriter.

I do my output with minimal formatting where each large object is on its own line. I currently do this by flushing the writer and then writing a new line to the stream.

If people want to do their own formatting then maybe there also could be a WriteIndent() method with ways to change the indent level.

Hi, I would like to learn and try this, but not sure if we have decided to be able to change based on description in this issue ?
Also during learning related code, I just found and raised another clearer and straightforward [issue](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/75075) about json comment, about which I have raised [PR](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/75074), could anyone help have a look at it also? thanks.

@eiriktsarpalis @layomia I'm fine with this breaking change considering this change should not break any parsers and I'm guessing most of the people who see comments formatted this way will be rather annoyed.

@lateapexearlyspeed send a patch and it will be easier to discuss it there. If the change will end up super complicated for whatever reason we might decide against it but honestly I doubt it and this looks like reasonable breaking change.
Curious why we think this is a breaking change? AFAIK JSON doesn't have whitespace significance so adding newlines to a formatting style shouldn't technically break anything.

@eiriktsarpalis I have mixed feeling as well. I think this originated from https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/52408#issuecomment-915754546

I'm ok with not reporting this as breaking change I guess but would be good to have description ready if we in fact somehow break someone and need to document it
Unless anybody disagrees, I think we can remove the breaking change labels.

review_comments: Per my comment above, would it be possible to include a couple of smoke tests that check indentation against a couple of string literals rather than constructing the expected string using test logic? Both might contain bugs or could regress.
Agreed, I'm looking at the test and it's really hard to figure out at first glance what this test is actually testing. I'd prefer couple of hardcoded string cases as well

Even I agree :) Changed to use string literal now.
Just note in advance when you view inside string literal result: 

> /*Comment in the middle of object*/,
> /*Comment in the middle of array*/,

This behavior is existing one, I did not change and just include them into test cases.
Both #75075 and #52408 should have be covered by test cases.

please add tests (even if throws exception), at minimum:
- testing behavior you added,
- comment in the beginning of file
- comment in the end of file
- comment in the beginning of the object
- comment in the middle of the object
- comment as last element of object
- same as above but array rather than object
honestly I'm not sure what's the intent of this method...

As [comment](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/75074#issuecomment-1247885991), previously we may need this helper method to instrument underlying stream to add additional newline and indented whitespaces during call newtonsoft.json methods because newtonsoft.json also did not do what proposal describes.
Really hard to tell just by looking at these tests, what format do we end up keeping in #75075?

For #75075, because it was closed without decision about format, so I picked this format based on [comment](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/75075#issue-1361510964):
> I just guess current difference is not intentional. If we should make them same, which one should we pick ?
> 
> I updated code to make them same as this one, please decide if another is better.
> 
> ```
> {
>   "property": 
>   /*comment*/"value"
> ```

Which is existing format of string parameter overload of `WriteCommentValue()`, and because it is no matter which type of property value, so this format should be more align with #52408 

Note this PR is to fix both #75075 and #52408, I just updated PR description now.
I see from the tests that this differs depending on whether the property value is a string or object. What is the exact rule being used here?

> I see from the tests that this differs depending on whether the property value is a string or object. What is the exact rule being used here?

The differ you found is just because current PR is to fix #52408. Current used rule is also based on those proposals, which is:

- for object and array: insert newlines between comment and object (or array), which is exactly described by #52408
- for other token types (not only string): keep existing behaviors not break (which were not to insert newline, as I understand), because #52408 doesn't  proposal behavior for them.

#75075 is to align 2 WriteCommentValue overload's different behavior about whether add newline between property name and comment, or not add newline. It is not related to property value currently because overload's difference is not there.

Current PR code should have been implemented based on rule above.
Is there a test for writing comment twice in a row?

Added.
There was already test case '[WriteCommentsInvalidTextAllowed](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e1ddbca5a008b4b15e8e6b309cbab12ba8b9b842/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/tests/System.Text.Json.Tests/Utf8JsonWriterTests.cs#L4154)' which wrote multiple comments in same line (so make sure behavior is not broken), but still added here for visible version. @krwq

optional suggestion: rename `_commentAfterNoneOrPropertyName` to `_forceNewLineAfterComment` - it took me a while to figure out what this code does - I think with the suggested name it makes it more obvious.
